name: Aman Kyoto
insider_take: Hidden within a secret garden where ancient temples whisper stories of old Japan, this ultra-luxe sanctuary feels like discovering a forgotten imperial retreat.
whats_special: Nestled in a 32-hectare forest at the foot of Hidari Daimonji mountain, Aman Kyoto occupies the same sacred grounds where Oda Nobunaga once strategized his conquest of Japan. The property features natural hot spring baths fed by the mountain's mineral-rich waters, while each pavilion offers private gardens designed using traditional Japanese principles dating back 400 years.
pro_tip: Book the Living Pavilion with Washitsu - it features the resort's only traditional tatami room and sits closest to the mountain hiking trails that lead to hidden Shinto shrines locals rarely share with tourists.
dont_miss: The pre-dawn forest meditation walks guided by a local monk, available only to Aman guests. Also, the hotel's tea ceremony performed using 16th-century utensils in the glass pavilion overlooking the mossy stone garden - it's conducted by one of Kyoto's few remaining traditional tea masters.
pros: Stunning traditional Japanese architecture seamlessly integrated with modern luxury
Exceptional service with personalized attention and cultural expertise
Tranquil forest setting providing complete privacy and serenity
Authentic Japanese cultural experiences including tea ceremonies and garden meditation
cons: Secluded location requires transportation to central Kyoto attractions
